intro: Dishwashing builds speed, machine handling and teamwork in a busy kitchen. The closest of the 25 careers below is laundry and dry-cleaning work, with an 84% skill match, but 22 of the 25 options pay more than the $34,810 dishwashers earn, and almost none need extra schooling.
why_it_works: A dish station keeps a whole kitchen running: you work fast, handle machines and chemicals safely and coordinate with cooks and servers. O*NET rates operation and control at 2.88 out of 5 for this job and coordination at 2.75. Factory, food production and delivery jobs use the same habits. The skills to build are analyzing how work flows and serving customers.
tips: Ask the kitchen to train you on prep work; food preparation is a step toward cook roles.
Mixing and blending machine operators earn $48,990, which is 41% more, in food and chemical plants.
A driver's license opens delivery work: light truck drivers earn $44,860, or 29% more.

faq.q: What jobs can former dishwashers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are laundry and dry-cleaning workers (84%), Food Preparation Workers (80%) and vehicle and equipment cleaners (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Packaging and filling machine operators are 76% matched and earn $43,220, which is 24% more than the $34,810 dishwasher median.

faq.q: Which careers for dishwashers pay more?
faq.a: 22 of the 25 matches pay more. Mixing and blending machine operators earn $48,990 (41% more), food roasting and baking machine operators $44,810 (29% more) and Light Truck Drivers $44,860 (29% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three train new workers on the job.

faq.q: Do dishwashers need more education to change jobs?
faq.a: No. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than dishwashers already have, including all of the top 10. In a close match, 70% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and training often takes a month or less.

The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, service orientation, complex problem solving and equipment selection. Time management already rates 2.62 out of 5 for dishwashers in O*NET, so learning to run machines or serve customers is the usual step up in pay.
